topic: CORRECTION: the SIMT-looking mnemonics are the model naming convention, not a compiler fallback
what_i_said_wrong: I reported that the simulated instruction stream being SIMT_LDK / SIMT_STG / SIMT_FFMA suggested the kernel had been lowered to a SIMT path instead of SimdVF

evidence_against_that.device_source: device_kernel.asc for the same model contains 93 simd_inst calls (vlds_unpack, vcvt, vmula, vadd, vcadd, vdupv, vdiv, vsqrt, vadds, vmuls, vsts_norm), so the generated code is unambiguously SimdVF
evidence_against_that.executed_instruction_count: the model executed 13925 instructions against an expected 15360 vector operations (4 rows x 6 iterations x (64 vld/convert/fma + 64 x 7 second-pass ops)), i.e. 91% of the expected body
evidence_against_that.conclusion: the SimdVF body did run. SIMT_* is just how this camodel names instructions that execute on the RVEC pipes; it is not a lowering fallback.

what_is_still_true.no_vector_names: the dump exposes no ISA-level vector mnemonics, so per-instruction analysis must be interpreted through the pipe column, not the mnemonic
what_is_still_true.code_regions_empty: code_exe.csv is empty because the kernel carries no debug_line information, so code-level attribution is unavailable
what_is_still_true.dma_unmodelled: MTE2 appears with a single instruction while the device reports DMA busy 27 percent on this model and 86-93 percent on the full kernel, so the simulator cannot be used to study the memory-bound behaviour

open_question: vector loads carry 514 cycles each on average, which looks like stall attribution rather than a real per-instruction cost. The isolated copy microbenchmark shows the same signature (913 cycles per load), so this metric may be an artefact. It must be validated by a controlled A/B before any conclusion is drawn from it.
status: tool runs and executes the real kernel; trustworthiness of its per-pipe numbers is still unestablished
